subject: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <security@forgeaxis.io>, compliance@covenantgrc.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration

Hi Lina and Covenant team,

Thanks for starting the conversation on the ForgeAxis integration. To keep procurement+assurance moving in parallel, we'd like to lock down a lightweight "artifact fingerprint" exchange playbook that lets our systems surface proof-of-evidence without shipping raw artifacts.

High-level proposal:
- Transport: push-based API (POST) with mutual auth (signed JWTs) or SFTP fallback
- Fingerprint format: sha256 hex + file size + logical artifact id
- Manifest fields: artifact_id, path, sha256, size_bytes, created_at, disposition (public/redacted/escrow)
- Retention hint: default 90 days; we can mark specific artifacts for long-term escrow

Can Covenant confirm manifest field constraints and whether a signed HMAC on the manifest is required for your ingestion pipeline? Attached is a quick artifact_map.csv stub mapping our internal artifact names -> canonical ids.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick alignment call this week (30m)
2) Exchange a draft SOW for API scope
3) Pilot: 1 customer pass (canary) with scoped artifacts

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- artifact_map.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Lina Park <security@forgeaxis.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@covenantgrc.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:45:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration

Jordan — thanks for the clear draft. ForgeAxis is aligned on the concept; a couple clarifying items:
- We prefer push API with short-lived signed JWTs. SFTP for backlog only.
- For ingestion we need either sha256 OR an HMAC (sha256 with a shared secret) on the manifest. HMAC is preferred for non-repudiation.
- Retention: ForgeAxis stores raw artifacts for 180 days by default; escrowed artifacts can be kept longer if contractually scoped.

Attaching our scoped_evidence_manifest.pdf (policy excerpt) and a brief timeline.

Lina
Director, Security Operations
ForgeAxis

Attachments:
- scoped_evidence_manifest.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration

Quick internal notes following Lina's reply:
- Implement manifest with both sha256 and an HMAC field (we'll compute HMAC with a per-partner secret). HMAC field name: manifest_hmac_sha256
- For transport, implement push API first. Plan SFTP ingestion for large historical dumps.
- Need decisions from infra/security on where we store raw artifacts (S3 escrow bucket) and KMS key for HMAC secrets.
- Requesting input from legal on retention >180 days escrow clauses.

Can Marcus own the infra tickets and Vanessa own the legal loop? I'll draft API specs and example payloads.

— Soojin
Senior Product Manager, Redwood

From: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@forgeaxis.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <security@forgeaxis.io>, compliance@covenantgrc.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration

Thanks — ForgeAxis prefers the following implementation details:
- Delivery: POST /ingest/artifacts with JSON manifest; authenticate with JWT signed by ForgeAxis private key; Redwood will verify using our public JWK.
- We can optionally accept pre-signed S3 URLs if payloads are >50MB.
- We will accept either simple sha256 OR an HMAC. We can do HMAC verification if Redwood submits the secret exchange via our in-portal key upload (we can support per-partner key rotation).

Attached: proposed SOW draft with deliverables and timeline.

Can we do a 30-min alignment tomorrow 11:00 PT? Also curious if Redwood plans to do any redaction prior to exchange — i.e., will you push raw artifacts or redacted versions + fingerprint?

Regards,
Ethan Ward
Head of Security Engineering
ForgeAxis

Attachments:
- sow-draft.docx (DOCX, 28KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ward <ethan.ward@forgeaxis.io>, Lina Park <security@forgeaxis.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Artifact fingerprint exchange playbook: ForgeAxis / Covenant GRC integration

Ethan / Lina — great, this aligns well.

Short answers:
- Redwood will push redacted artifacts by default; escrow raw artifacts only when the "disposition" field is set to escrow.
- We'll implement manifest with fields you requested plus manifest_hmac_sha256. We'll seed a per-partner HMAC secret via the ForgeAxis portal (or via a signed SFTP key exchange) and support rotation.
- Transport: API first, S3 presigned URLs for large files.

Action items and owners (canary timeline week 0 = contract signed):
1) Redwood: API spec + example payloads (So., Soojin) — due 2027-05-07
2) ForgeAxis: Key upload flow + JWT JWK publishing (Ethan) — due 2027-05-07
3) Infra: escrow S3 bucket + KMS keys (Marcus) — due 2027-05-10
4) Legal: retention clause and escrow SLAs (Vanessa) — due 2027-05-12
5) Pilot canary with one test customer (all) — week of 2027-05-17

Let's take the 11:00 PT slot tomorrow. I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference
